answer: Each identity needs a licensed ID check plus a live selfie: the applicant submits a government ID to an independent verifier, which returns a signed hash. A 30-second liveness selfie is matched to the ID photo; a mismatch fails closed. The hash enters the registry once; a second application with the same hash is rejected, sealing karst-like gaps where one person spawns many accounts. A forger needs 1,000 distinct real IDs at $12 each, or $12,000, plus 1,000 live faces. Like onyx, each identity is one stone no forger can split, and a falcon-fast check keeps every stone in sight.
